description: Fetch a complete Q&A thread — question body and all answers, accepted answer first then sorted by score, rendered as clean markdown with fenced code blocks. Accepts a full Stack Exchange question URL, which is read from the site its host names (e.g. "https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/88490/how-do-i-use-a-heredoc"), or an integer question ID read from site (e.g. "11227809"). HTML is normalized to markdown automatically; attribution (author + link) included per CC BY-SA 4.0. Get question IDs from stackexchange_search_questions or stackexchange_get_tag_faq.

includeComments.description: Fetch the comment thread under the question and under every returned answer (default false). Comments are where a stale answer usually gets corrected ("this breaks on v3", "use X instead now"), so set this when the answer's continued accuracy matters. Costs 2 extra API calls against the daily quota regardless of how many answers are returned.

maxAnswers.description: Maximum number of answers to include (1–100, default 10). Answers are sorted: accepted first, then by score.

questionIdOrUrl.description: Numeric question ID (e.g. "11227809") or a full Stack Exchange question URL (e.g. "https://stackoverflow.com/questions/11227809/why-is-processing-a-sorted-array-faster"). A URL carries its own site: the question is read from the URL's host, so question IDs from any Stack Exchange site resolve correctly. A URL whose host is not a Stack Exchange site is read from site when one is given, and fails as invalid_site otherwise.

site.description: Stack Exchange site a numeric question ID belongs to — the api_site_parameter (e.g. "stackoverflow", "unix") or the site's domain (e.g. "unix.stackexchange.com"). Defaults to "stackoverflow". Not needed with a URL, which names its own site: a site naming a different one is ignored, or used when the URL host is not a Stack Exchange site, and either way reported as siteConflict. Call stackexchange_list_sites to discover valid values.

name: stackexchange_get_thread

acceptedAnswerId.description: ID of the accepted answer when one exists.

answerCount.description: Total answers the question has upstream. When greater than the returned answers[] length, more answers exist — raise maxAnswers to fetch them.

answers.description: Answers sorted: accepted answer first, then by score descending.

items.description: A single Q&A answer with markdown body, score, dates, and author attribution.

authorLink.description: Answer author profile URL when available.

authorName.description: Answer author display name when available.

authorUserId.description: Answer author numeric user ID when available — pass to stackexchange_get_user to fetch the full profile.

bodyMarkdown.description: Answer body normalized from HTML to markdown.

comments.description: Comments on this answer, newest first, present only when includeComments is true. An empty array means this post has no comments; an absent array means its comment state is unknown — either comments were not requested, or the batched fetch was cut short before this post contributed any. Never read an absent array as "no comments".

items.description: A single comment with markdown body, score, date, and author attribution.

authorLink.description: Comment author profile URL when available.

authorName.description: Comment author display name when available.

bodyMarkdown.description: Comment body normalized from HTML to markdown.

creationDate.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the comment was posted — the newest comments carry the freshest corrections.

score.description: Comment score — comments can score below zero.

commentsTruncated.description: True when this answer's comments[] is a partial list — more exist upstream than were returned.

creationDate.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the answer was posted — an old answer may predate the current API.

isAccepted.description: True when this is the accepted answer.

lastActivityDate.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent edit or activity on the answer.

authorLink.description: Question author profile URL when available.

authorName.description: Question author display name when available.

authorUserId.description: Question author numeric user ID when available — pass to stackexchange_get_user to fetch the full profile.

bodyMarkdown.description: Question body normalized from HTML to markdown.

cap.description: The maxAnswers cap applied to this request.

comments.description: Comments on the question, newest first, present only when includeComments is true. An empty array means this post has no comments; an absent array means its comment state is unknown — either comments were not requested, or the batched fetch was cut short before this post contributed any. Never read an absent array as "no comments".

items.description: A single comment with markdown body, score, date, and author attribution.

authorLink.description: Comment author profile URL when available.

authorName.description: Comment author display name when available.

bodyMarkdown.description: Comment body normalized from HTML to markdown.

creationDate.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the comment was posted — the newest comments carry the freshest corrections.

score.description: Comment score — comments can score below zero.

commentsCap.description: Maximum comments carried per post — a post at this count reports commentsTruncated.

commentsTruncated.description: True when the question's comments[] is a partial list — more exist upstream than were returned.

creationDate.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the question was asked — use it to judge whether the advice is still current.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `question_not_found`: The question lookup returns an empty result set — SE returns HTTP 200 with no items for unknown question IDs rather than 404. `invalid_site`: The site value, or the host of a question URL, is not a Stack Exchange network site. `invalid_id_or_url`: The input is neither an integer ID nor text holding a /questions/{id} path, or Stack Exchange refused the ID. `invalid_parameter`: Stack Exchange rejected a request parameter other than the question ID, and named the field. `quota_exceeded`: The Stack Exchange API quota_remaining has reached 0. `throttled`: Stack Exchange is throttling this server's IP address, or its backoff window outlasts what the call can wait. `pacer_shed`: The call would wait in this server's queue to Stack Exchange longer than its time budget allows. `invalid_api_key`: Stack Exchange does not recognize the API key this server is configured with. `upstream_unavailable`: Stack Exchange reported itself temporarily unavailable or failing internally, or answered with a body that is not the expected JSON envelope. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

lastActivityDate.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent activity on the question (edit, answer, or comment).

questionId.description: Numeric question ID — identifies this thread on the site.

quotaMax.description: Maximum API quota calls per day (300 keyless, ~10,000 with API key).

quotaRemaining.description: Remaining API quota calls for the current day.

siteConflict.description: Present only when questionIdOrUrl is a URL and site names a different site — says which of the two the question was read from.

resolvedBy.description: Which one the question was read from: "url_host" when site was ignored in favor of the URL's own site, "site" when the URL host is not a Stack Exchange site and site was used instead.

items.description: A tag applied to this question.

truncated.description: True when answers were capped at maxAnswers.
